app.title: सखा (Sakha) - The Sanskrit Parser
app.summary: A person pastes or types a passage in any of twenty Roman or Indic scripts, picks a parsing model, a dictionary and an output script, and presses Analyze. The interface works out the input script, plays the passage aloud, and breaks it into syllables and letters with counts of vowels and consonants. It then splits the passage into its separate words by undoing the sound changes at word boundaries, and lists every word with its base form and its grammatical tags. Each base form links to a dictionary entry and each verb links to a root index. A separate embeddable script does the word splitting for any stretch of text a reader selects on another website.

task.text: Split a passage of Sanskrit into its words and give each word's base form and grammatical analysis, so a reader can follow the text word by word.

data.text: A short passage of text in one of many scripts. It is normalised to one romanisation, split into sentences at the danda marks, and returned as a sequence of words, each with a base form and morphological tags.
data.item: a word in a sentence of the passage, with its base form and grammatical tags

stage.text: analysing a passage word by word while reading a classical text

mechanism.text: Sidebar settings choose the model, the dictionary, the language of the interface and the input and output scripts, and they shape every result. One Analyze press over the text box fills in, top to bottom, an audio player, a collapsible panel of syllable and letter counts, the split words as one line, and a table with one row per word that links out to dictionaries. A separate page plugin shows the split words in a tooltip under any text the reader selects.

field.text: word segmentation and morphological tagging in Sanskrit computational linguistics

workflow.name: split a text into units and tag each unit's grammar

steps.here: Paste or type a passage into the text box. The input script is detected automatically or chosen from a list, and the text is converted to IAST before parsing.

steps.step: choose how the analysis runs and how results are shown
steps.here: The sidebar picks the model (Dharmamitra gives full morphology; Hellwig gives segmentation only), the dictionary for lemma links, the output script, and English or Sanskrit for the interface.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Analyze voices the passage with a Flite voice file and breaks it into aksharas (syllables) and vinyāsa (spelling). It also counts svaras (vowels), vyañjanas (consonants), varṇas (letters) and total characters.

steps.step: split the text into its units
steps.here: The text is split into sentences at the dandas and sent to the chosen model. The model undoes the sandhi (sound changes at word boundaries), and the words come back as one line in the output script.

A numbered table gives each word with its lemma and its grammar. The tags are rewritten in Pāṇinian terms: lakāra (tense and mood), case, number, gender, and parasmaipada or ātmanepada (the verb's voice).

steps.step: look an item up in a reference
steps.here: Each lemma links to the chosen dictionary (Kosha.app, Ambuda or Sanskrit Kosha), and each verb links to a search in the ashtadhyayi.com root index.

distinctive: Word boundaries are hidden by sandhi, so splitting the words means undoing those sound changes before any tagging
The model's raw tags are corrected by rules taken from traditional grammar: word-initial a or ā for past tenses, suffixes for the benedictive, and endings for ātmanepada voice
Input and output can each be any of twenty Roman or Indic scripts, with the input script detected automatically
The whole interface can switch to Sanskrit, with Devanagari numerals and danda punctuation
An embeddable plugin gives the same word split in a tooltip under text a reader selects on any website
